title: Accordion
description: Lets you show and hide content, on its own or as a group.

title: Anchor
description: A structural primitive to enable CSS Anchor Positioning on stuff.

title: Avatar
description: Avatars show a person or entity as an image, initials or icon.

title: Badge
description: Badges attach a small count or status dot to another element.

title: Button group
description: Groups related buttons.

title: Button
description: Buttons allow users to take actions, and make choices, with a single tap.

title: Callout
description: Callouts call out for user attention. Should be part of the flow and used without interrupting the user's task.
keywords: alert banner message box notice warning

title: Card
description:
The card is extremely versatile and can be used on its own, or as a building
    block for accordions, dialogs and more.

title: Carousel
description: A scrolling list with snap points, buttons and markers.

title: Checkbox
description:
Use a Checkbox for choices that are submitted with a form. For a setting
    that applies right away, use a Switch, and for options in a toolbar a Toggle. See also: Checkbox field group.

title: Chip
description:
Chips are compact elements that represent an input, attribute, or action.
    Use them for filters, tags and choices. For the main action, like Save or
    Send, use a Button.

title: Command
description: A search input above a list of links and actions that it filters as you type.
keywords: autocomplete combobox command palette filter quick open search

title: Copy
description: A button that copies text or a field's value to the clipboard.

title: Description list
description: Description lists are used to display a list of terms and their descriptions.

title: Dialog
description: A minimally styled window overlaid on the main content. By design the Dialog is minimal with zero content to allow for both modal and non-modal use.

title: Divider
description: It's just a line.

title: Drawer
description:
Slides in from the sides, top or bottom of the screen. Good for navigation,
    filters and side content. For a question or a short task that needs the
    user's full attention, use a Dialog.

title: Form
description: Spacing and grouping for form fields.

title: Layout
description:
Six classes for the space between components: .ui-layout-column,
    .ui-layout-row, .ui-layout-grid, .ui-layout-columns, .ui-layout-media and .ui-layout-container. Put
    them on wrapper elements, such as div, section or
    ul. They sit in the utils layer, so on a component they
    replace its own layout. Their gaps come from the --ui-space-* scale, so they follow --ui-space-scale.

title: List
description: Lists are continuous, vertical indexes of text and images and video. Use lists to help users find a specific item and act on it.

title: Menu
description: A popover list of actions or links.

title: Message
description: Chat bubbles that group by sender, with attachments, reactions and a typing indicator.

title: Number field
description: A number field with buttons that step the value down and up, for amounts like a quantity.

title: One-time code
description: A one-time password (OTP) field: one input drawn as a box per character, with paste and SMS autofill.

title: Progress
description: See also: Spinner.

title: Radio
description: See also: Form documentation.

title: Range
description: Range lets users pick a number by sliding a thumb along a track.

title: Rating
description: A star rating: a meter that shows a score, or radios that collect one.

title: Select
description:
Leverages the List component to provide markup for the Select popover. Use a Select to pick a value in a
    form. For actions, use a Menu.

title: Spinner
description:
Add it to an element with aria-busy="true". Spinners are always
    indeterminate. See also: Progress bar.

title: 1. Because it's blocked by another use case
Stat
description: A stat shows one number with its label and the change behind it.

title: Stepper
description: Shows where someone is in a flow of steps, such as a checkout.

title: Switch
description: Use a Switch for a setting that applies right away. Use a Checkbox for choices that are submitted with a form, and a Toggle for options in a toolbar. See also: Switch field group.

title: Table
description: Displays tabular data. Basic tables with row and column headers, and optional captions and footers.

title: Tabs
description:
The Tabs are radio inputs and the Panels are just divs that show and hide
    based on the radio inputs' :checked state. Use Tabs to switch between
    panels of content. To pick an option, like a list or grid view, use a Toggle group.

title: Text field
description: An input for single-line text data. Basic text fields with labels, field descriptions, and validation states.
keywords: email input password search text box

title: Textarea
description: An input for multi-line text data. Basic textareas with labels, supporting text, and validation states.

title: Timeline
description: A list of dated events with markers and a connecting line.

title: Toast
description: Short messages that confirm an action and dismiss themselves.

title: Toggle
description: Toggle buttons and toggle groups switch options on and off, alone or as a set.

title: Tooltip
description:
Built on top of Anchor.
    
    
      
        Wrap the trigger in <Tooltip> and pass a stable{" "}
        id. Set interestfor with that id on the trigger
        element itself (it only works on real invokers like{" "}
        <button> or <a>). Put the tooltip
        in
        TooltipContent after the trigger.

title: Typography
description:
Styles for headings, body text, and other text content. Use util classes
    anywhere or wrap content in .ui-rich-text.

title: Accessibility
description:
A few basics to get you started. OPUI leans on native HTML, so a lot comes
    for free, but you still decide the names, the order and the content. Test
    with a keyboard and a screen reader, it always depends.

title: Acknowledgments
description:
Open Props UI stands on a lot of shoulders. These are the people, projects
    and resources that made it possible.

title: Browser support
description:
The web platform features the components rely on, and the browsers that ship
    each one.

title: Concepts
description:
The architecture: cascade layers, token tiers, scopes, props and classes,
    naming, rich text, and where JavaScript is still needed.

title: Customizing
description:
Where your CSS goes: a theme in theme.custom changes the whole library,
    a component's --_* properties change one component or one instance,
    and your own layer holds the rest.

title: Migrating from v5 to v6
description:
The breaking changes in v6 and how to update your code, component by
    component.

title: Theme tokens
description:
Every token theme.css and core/palette.css declare,
    with its default and its tier, and the instance inputs components read. Most are roles; the others are
    marked knob, primitive, hook, component
    or input. The tests check every promised contrast ratio in light
    and dark mode, with and without more contrast.

title: Theming
description:
The knobs and roles behind colors, density, spacing, corners, fonts,
    elevation, motion and contrast, and the classes that scope them.

title: Why Open Props UI?
description:
Components built from the HTML and CSS the platform ships today, as files
    you can read, copy and own.

title: Getting started
description:
OPUI ships first-class React 19 components. Install the package, import what
    you need, and you're set.

title: An accordion that animates to auto
description: interpolate-size and ::details-content let a details element transition to its natural height.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback interpolate-size JavaScript that measures the content and animates a pixel height. `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` and `::details-content` transition a `<details>` to its natural height. details-content interpolate-size

title: Hover cards without JavaScript
description: interestfor, popover=hint and anchor positioning open a hover card on hover and focus.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback interestfor Timers for hover intent, focus and blur listeners, and a positioning library that measures and flips the card. `interestfor` and `popover="hint"` open it on hover and focus, and anchor positioning places it. anchor-positioning interest-invokers popover-hint

title: Squircle avatars with corner-shape
description: aspect-ratio, :has(img) and corner-shape for avatars.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback corner-shape An SVG mask or a `clip-path` path: a fixed shape that clips borders and shadows too. `corner-shape: squircle` draws the corner, and `aspect-ratio: 1` keeps the avatar square. aspect-ratio corner-shape has

title: One Button, no IconButton
description: :has(> svg:only-child) turns any Button into an icon button.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback Gotchas :has() A separate `IconButton` component or an `iconOnly` prop, with every size and variant built twice. `:has(> svg:only-child)` lets the button see that it only holds an icon. has

title: Severity colors from one source color
description: Relative colors and light-dark() derive every severity shade from one color.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback oklch(from …) 40 hand-picked colors for five severities in two schemes, or a preprocessor that only works at build time. One `--ui-palette-source` per severity, and `oklch(from …)` derives every shade. light-dark relative-color

title: A carousel made of CSS
description: Scroll snap, ::scroll-button() and ::scroll-marker: a carousel without JavaScript.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback ::scroll-button() JavaScript that listens to scroll events to run the buttons and dots, with their accessibility done by hand. `::scroll-button()` and `::scroll-marker` generate focusable buttons and dots. scroll-buttons scroll-markers scroll-snap

title: Drawing a checkbox
description: appearance: none, a clip-path checkmark and system colors for a native checkbox.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback appearance: none A hidden input and a fake box with an SVG check that mirrors every state. `appearance: none` lets the real input draw its own box and check. appearance clip-path

title: Leader lines with grid
description: A container query and a grid pseudo-element draw dotted leader lines.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback @container A row of clipped dots, a repeating background or an empty filler element, and a media query that only knows the viewport. A grid per pair with a dotted `::after` between term and description, and a container query for the column. container-queries

title: Dialogs without JavaScript
description: Invoker commands, closedby and @starting-style for modal dialogs.
headings: The problem The trick Keyboard shortcuts Try it Scroll lock Fallback closedby A click handler for `showModal()`, another for `close()`, and a backdrop listener that checks where the click landed. `commandfor`, `command` and `closedby` open and close it, `@starting-style` fades it in, and `allow-discrete` fades it out. dialog-closedby invoker-commands overlay starting-style transition-behavior

title: Sliding drawers with @starting-style
description: A dialog that slides in from any edge, and out again with allow-discrete.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback @starting-style A fixed `<div>` with JavaScript for the focus trap, Esc and backdrop clicks, and a class removed after `transitionend` to animate it out. A modal `<dialog>` that slides with `translate`, `@starting-style` and `allow-discrete`. overlay starting-style transition-behavior

title: Fluid type with progress()
description: progress() turns the viewport width into one 0 to 1 ramp that every heading size shares.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback progress() A clamp() per heading with a hand-tuned vi slope, so every heading grew over a different range of viewport widths. `progress(100vi, start, end)` is one shared ramp, and each heading mixes its two steps with it. progress-function

title: Smarter fieldsets with :has()
description: :has() lets fieldsets and legends style themselves from what they contain.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback :has(:required) Modifier classes or props kept in sync with what the fieldset contains. `:has()` lets the fieldset and legend style themselves from their content. has

title: Menus with popover and anchor positioning
description: Popover, invoker commands and anchor positioning: a menu with no JavaScript.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback popover JavaScript to toggle and dismiss it, `z-index` fights, and a positioning library that measures and flips. `popover`, invoker commands and anchor positioning, with the trigger as the implicit anchor. anchor-positioning invoker-commands popover

title: Styling the native progress bar
description: appearance: none and :indeterminate on the native progress element.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback :indeterminate A `<div role="progressbar">` with its ARIA attributes kept in sync by hand. The native `<progress>` with `appearance: none`, so the role and the value stay native. appearance container-style-queries indeterminate

title: Range sliders with datalist ticks
description: A scroll-driven gradient fill and datalist tick marks for input range.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback <datalist> Vendor pseudo-elements, a fill only Firefox could draw, and tick labels that never showed. A scroll-driven animation on the thumb fills the track, and `display: flex` brings the `<datalist>` labels back. datalist input-range scroll-driven-animations

title: opui 6.0
description: What changed in 6.0 and why, with live demos.
headings: It's a proper design system now Four example themes Token tiers Contrast as a guarantee Loads of new components So much cool stuff in the docs Blocks! Theme builder The CSS is the component Slots become parts, props get one naming model The platform did the work Browser support, honestly The new "by hand" Where it landed Migrating

title: A select you can style
description: appearance: base-select, ::picker(select) and :open for a fully styled select.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback base-select A rebuilt listbox: a button, a popup, ARIA roles and JavaScript for focus, keyboard and typeahead. `appearance: base-select` makes the real `<select>` stylable, with `<selectedcontent>` and `::picker(select)`. customizable-select open-pseudo

title: Spinners from aria-busy
description: aria-busy=true is all it takes to show a spinner.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback aria-busy A spinner class for sighted users and `aria-busy` for assistive technology, kept in sync. `[aria-busy="true"]` is the only switch, and a `::before` ring spins. animations-css not

title: A switch from a checkbox
description: A native checkbox, appearance: none and an outline trick.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback appearance: none A `<button>` with `aria-checked` toggled in JavaScript, or a hidden checkbox plus extra spans. `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">` with `appearance: none` draws its own track and dot. appearance light-dark

title: A header that knows it's stuck
description: scroll-state() container queries give a stuck table header and a scrolled dialog their shadows.
headings: The problem The trick Scroll shadows Try it Fallback scroll-state() A scroll listener, or an `IntersectionObserver` with a sentinel element. `container-type: scroll-state` and `@container scroll-state(stuck: block-start)` show the shadow. anchor-positioning container-scroll-state-queries

title: Tabs from radio buttons
description: Radio inputs, order and :nth-child(of S) for CSS-only tabs.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback :nth-child(of S) JavaScript for clicks, `aria-selected` and panels, or CSS tabs with one selector per tab. One radio group, and `:checked + label + panel` shows the right panel. nth-child-of

title: Validation that waits with :user-invalid
description: :user-invalid shows errors after the user interacts, not on page load.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback :user-invalid JavaScript that adds a touched class on blur. `:user-invalid` only matches after the user has changed the field. user-pseudos

title: Textareas that grow with field-sizing
description: field-sizing: content and lh units for auto-growing textareas.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback field-sizing JavaScript that resets the height to `scrollHeight` on every keystroke. `field-sizing: content` grows and shrinks the textarea with its text. field-sizing lh

title: Tooltips with interestfor
description: interestfor, calc-size() and @position-try for tooltips that stay on screen.
headings: The problem The trick Staying on screen Try it Fallback interestfor Event listeners, delays and a positioning library that measures and flips. `interestfor` and `popover="hint"` open it on hover and focus, and anchor positioning keeps it on screen. anchor-positioning calc-size interest-invokers popover-hint

title: Under the hood
description: Every component, built one step at a time. Pick a step and the demo runs only the CSS up to it.

title: Vertical rhythm with round()
description: round() snaps line heights and font sizes to a rhythm step.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback round() A Sass function per font size, which breaks once sizes are fluid. `round(up, value, step)` snaps every line height to the grid at computed time. registered-custom-properties round-mod-rem

title: Accordion Actions API
description: Reference for Accordion Actions React component.
terms: AccordionActions A group of actions, such as buttons. align Alignment for the actions.

title: Accordion Summary API
description: Reference for Accordion Summary React component.
terms: AccordionSummary The always visible header. The marker. Renders a chevron by default. Only `.ui-marker` animates. marker

title: Accordion API
description: Reference for Accordion React component.
terms: Accordion Container element. The always visible header. The marker. In Astro, React, Svelte and Vue, `AccordionSummary` renders a chevron by default. Only `.ui-marker` animates. The collapsible content. A group of actions, such as buttons. name Groups accordions so only one of them can be open at a time. markerAnimation How the marker animates when the accordion opens. `rotate` turns it upside down, `flip` mirrors it, and `turn` gives a chevron that points to the inline end a quarter turn, so it points down when open. open Whether the accordion is open. variant The variant to use. The default `plain` accordion has the page surface and no border, like a Card. `transparent` has no surface, border or padding.

title: Anchor API
description: Reference for Anchor React component.
terms: Anchor Container element. Scopes the anchor to its content. The content the floating content is anchored to. The floating content. id The id of the root. With `trigger="hover"`, the id of `AnchorContent`. Add `interestfor` with the same id to the trigger. Required with `trigger="hover"`. positionArea Any valid `position-area` value. Controls where the floating content is placed. The `self-` keywords follow the content's own direction, so the placement mirrors in a right-to-left part of a left-to-right page. trigger Shows the floating content on hover and focus with `popover="hint"`. Without it, the content always shows.

title: Avatar Group API
description: Reference for Avatar Group React component.
terms: AvatarGroup A group of overlapping avatars.

title: Avatar API
description: Reference for Avatar React component.
terms: Avatar Container element. The avatar image. src alt alt Alternative text for the image. Required with `src`. Use an empty string when the name is shown next to it. as The element to render. Defaults to `"a"` with `href`. disabled Disables a button avatar. A link avatar drops its `href` and gets `aria-disabled="true"` instead. href The link to use. Renders an `<a>`. shape The shape of the avatar. size The size of the element. src The image source. Replaces the content. variant The variant to use. `filled` is the primary color, `tonal` its tint and `outlined` the border color with no fill.

title: Badge API
description: Reference for Badge React component.
terms: Badge Container element. The element the badge is anchored to. default The indicator, inside `.ui-floating`. Holds `label`, the visible text with `hideLabel`, or only screen reader text with `dot`. label indicator color Optional colors. corner The corner the indicator sits on. dot Renders the indicator as a dot. `label` stays as screen reader text, and the `indicator` slot isn't shown. hideLabel Hides `label` visually, for the whole sentence screen readers read, such as "5 unread messages". The `indicator` slot then holds the visible text and is hidden from screen readers. invisible Hides the indicator.

title: Button Group API
description: Reference for Button Group React component.
terms: ButtonGroup Container element. The buttons and button links. default color Optional colors for the buttons. orientation The orientation of the element. overflow What the items do when they don't fit. `"wrap"` wraps them onto more rows, `"scroll"` keeps them on one row and scrolls it sideways, and `"shrink"` keeps them on one row and truncates labels with an ellipsis. Icon-only items keep their size. size The size of the buttons. variant The variant of the buttons.

title: Button API
description: Reference for Button React component.
terms: Button Container element. An optional icon. An optional keyboard hint. aria-label The accessible name, for a button without visible text. React and Svelte require it, or `aria-labelledby`, when there are no `children`. aria-labelledby The id of the element that names a button without visible text, instead of `aria-label`. as The element to render. Defaults to `"a"` with `href`. color Optional colors. disabled Disables the button. A link button drops its `href` and gets `aria-disabled="true"`. href The link to use. Renders an `<a>`. round Fully rounded corners, a circle when icon-only. size The size of the element. variant The variant to use.

title: Callout API
description: Reference for Callout React component.
terms: Callout Container element. An optional icon before the content. In Astro, React, Svelte and Vue, `CalloutIcon` renders the default one for info, success, warning and critical. The content, with an optional heading first. severity The severity. Sets the color, and in Astro, React, Svelte and Vue the icon `CalloutIcon` renders. variant The variant to use.

title: Card Actions API
description: Reference for Card Actions React component.
terms: CardActions A group of actions, such as buttons. align Alignment for the actions.

title: Card API
description: Reference for Card React component.
terms: Card Container element. The card header. The card content. A group of actions, such as buttons. density How much room the parts get. `spacious` pads them with `--ui-space-5` for a card that stands alone, such as a sign-in form, `dense` with `--ui-space-2` for a small stat. variant The variant to use. The default `plain` card has the page surface color and no border.

title: Carousel API
description: Reference for Carousel React component.
terms: Carousel The scroller. An item. default The previous button. `::scroll-button(block-start)` when vertical. buttons The next button. `::scroll-button(block-end)` when vertical. buttons A marker, one per item. markers align Where items snap. aria-label Accessible name of the carousel. aspectRatio Aspect ratio that images, videos and iframes are cropped to. buttons Previous and next buttons. `"outside"` places them beside the items, and `"none"` leaves them out. itemsPerView Number of visible items. markers One marker per item, after the list. orientation The orientation of the element. A vertical carousel is `--_block-size` tall, `24rem` by default. peek Shows part of the neighboring items. persistentButtons Keeps the buttons visible at the ends. A disabled button has a muted border. stretch Makes each item a grid, so its content (a card, a link) fills the item's height. Media with an aspect ratio keeps it.

title: Checkbox Input API
description: Reference for Checkbox Input React component.
terms: CheckboxInput The checkbox input, without a label. indeterminate Shows a partially checked state. Sets the `indeterminate` property on the `<input>`.

title: Checkbox API
description: Reference for Checkbox React component.
terms: Checkbox Container element. The checkbox input. The label. label default Supporting text displayed below the label. endText end-text card Renders the checkbox as a card: a padded, outlined surface that tints when hovered and when checked, with the label and `endText` inside. Add `spread` to put the input at the end, and `variant` to change the surface. disabled Dims the checkbox and shows a not-allowed cursor. `aria-disabled="true"` looks the same, but keeps the checkbox focusable and its value in the form, and doesn't stop the change, so block it with a script. error Marks the control invalid and shows error styles. hideLabel Visually hides the label, `.ui-sr-only` instead of `.ui-label`. id The id of the `<input>`. indeterminate Shows a partially checked state. Sets the `indeterminate` property on the `<input>`. name The name of the `<input>`. Inside a `FieldGroup`, the group's `name` applies. orientation The orientation of the element. `vertical` stacks the label under the input. required Adds a required mark after the label. The form won't submit until it's checked. size The size of the element. spread Pushes the label and the input to opposite ends. value The value of the `<input>`, submitted with the form when it's checked. variant The surface of the card, with `card`. `outlined` has a border, `tonal` a tinted surface and `elevated` a shadow, like Card.

title: Chip API
description: Reference for Chip React component.
terms: Chip Container element. Can be a `<div>`, `<a>` or `<button>`. Optional content at the start, such as an icon. start The label, text or rich content. label label Optional content at the end, such as an icon. end as The element to render. Defaults to `"a"` with `href`. disabled Disables a button chip. A link chip drops its `href` and gets `aria-disabled="true"` instead. dot Adds a leading dot in the chip's color. `critical`, `warning` and `neutral` shape it. href The link to use. Renders an `<a>`. multiline Lets the label wrap to multiple lines. severity The severity of a status chip. It tints the chip, and colors and shapes its dot. size The size of the element. variant The variant to use.

title: Command Group API
description: Reference for Command Group React component.
terms: CommandGroup A labeled group of options in the `CommandList`. The label, shown above the options. label label The options, a transparent `List` of list items with a link or a button each. label The group's label, which names the group.

title: Command API
description: Reference for Command React component.
terms: Command The `<opui-command>` custom element, a column with the input above the options. The search icon and the input, which the element makes a combobox. A button with `command="--copy"` copies the value of its first `input` or `textarea`, or else its text without buttons and popovers. Without the Clipboard API, or when it refuses or takes longer than a second, it copies through a selection, and where that is blocked too it selects the text instead. The live region that announces the copy, visually hidden with `.ui-sr-only`. The label next to the button, in the look of an outlined button at the button's height. An event, with its marker and the line to the next one. items The items, as `{ color, current, datetime, description, headingLevel, label, time }` objects. `description` renders a paragraph. size The size of the element. tracked Colors the line and the plain markers before the current item with the primary color, like a progress tracker.

title: Toast API
description: Reference for Toast React component.
terms: Toaster The `<opui-toaster>` custom element, with `display: contents`. A button with `commandfor` and `command="--toast"` shows a toast with its `data-toast` text and `data-toast-severity`, and `toast(message, { action, duration, severity })` or `toast.success(message)` does it from a script, where `action` takes a `label` and an `onClick`. `dismiss(toast)` returns a promise that resolves once the toast is gone. The stack of toasts, a manual popover at the block end and the inline end of the viewport unless `side` and `align` move it. It opens with the first toast and closes after the last. A toast, a `Callout` with the severity class, its icon, the message in `.ui-content`, an action `Button` when it has an `action`, and a close `Button`. The element adds it, and on dismiss makes it `inert`, fades it out and closes its gap before it removes it. The live region that announces each toast, visually hidden with `.ui-sr-only` and outside the popover, so it's always in the page. align Where the toasts sit along their side of the viewport. closeLabel The accessible name of the close button of each toast. duration How long a toast stays, in milliseconds, while the pointer and focus are elsewhere. id The id the buttons point at with `commandfor`. Required. side The side of the viewport the toasts sit on.

title: Toggle Button API
description: Reference for Toggle Button React component.
terms: ToggleButton Container element. A visually hidden checkbox or radio input. checked Selects the button. disabled Disables the button. id The id of the `<input>`. label The button text when there is no child content. name The name of the input. Set by the group. required The form won't submit until it's checked. A `ToggleGroup` without `multiple` needs it on one button only. size The size of the element. type The input type. `"radio"` allows one selection in a group. A `ToggleGroup` without `multiple` makes every button a radio. value The value of the input.

title: Toggle Group API
description: Reference for Toggle Group React component.
terms: ToggleGroup Container element. A toggle button. defaultValue The starting selection when `value` is omitted. multiple Lets several buttons be checked, with checkbox inputs. Without it, one button is checked at a time, with radio inputs in a `[role="radiogroup"]`. name The name shared by the inputs. Generated when omitted. onValueChange Called with the new selection when a button is toggled. orientation The orientation of the element. overflow What the items do when they don't fit. `"wrap"` wraps them onto more rows, `"scroll"` keeps them on one row and scrolls it sideways, and `"shrink"` keeps them on one row and truncates labels with an ellipsis. Icon-only items keep their size. size The size of the buttons. value The value of the checked button, or the values of the checked buttons with `multiple`.

title: Tooltip API
description: Reference for Tooltip React component.
terms: Tooltip Container element. The trigger that shows the tooltip on hover and focus. The tooltip, a `popover="hint"`. arrow Adds an arrow that points to the trigger. id The id of the tooltip. Add `interestfor` with the same id to the trigger, and on a toggletip `commandfor` and `command="toggle-popover"` too. Required. positionArea Any valid `position-area` value. Controls where the tooltip is placed. The `self-` keywords follow the tooltip's own direction, so the placement mirrors in a right-to-left part of a left-to-right page.

title: Typography API
description: Reference for Typography React component.
terms: Typography Classless typography for uncontrolled child markup. blockquote Quoted block with a start border. caption Muted supporting text. codeBlock Monospace preformatted block. color Tone of `.ui-swatch`, and the text color of `.ui-p`, `.ui-caption` and `.ui-overline`. Without it, the swatch takes the palette accent of the scope it sits in. heading Heading styles for any element. headingGroup Groups an overline, heading, and optional body copy. icon Sizes an inline `svg` to `--ui-icon-size` and keeps it from shrinking in a flex row. inline Inline text element utilities. link Link styles outside `.ui-rich-text`. On hover and focus, the underline gets thicker. The color gets darker in light mode and lighter in dark mode. notRichText Ends the `.ui-rich-text` styles inside it. overline Small uppercase label text. paragraph Body paragraph styling. size Size modifiers on `.ui-p` and `.ui-icon`. An icon reads `--ui-icon-size-small` and `--ui-icon-size-large`. tabularNums Digits of one width, so numbers line up in a column of prices or stats. swatch A small colored dot for a legend, in `--_swatch-bg-color`, the palette accent of its tone or scope.
